jobs.name: Morning operator report
jobs.prompt:
You are doing the user's proactive daily morning stand-up/operator report in Discord.

Use the loaded `operator-morning-reports` skill as a tone guide, but apply the user's latest corrections below. Keep it laconic, skimmable, Discord-native, no Markdown tables, no long essays.

A pre-run script may inject Google Workspace context above this prompt. Treat that injected output as read-only source material from these five profiles:
- `hermes-agent` / trapiistan@gmail.com — Hermes/YouTube/operator account
- `personal-main` / Affan.fareed@gmail.com — personal main, read-focused
- `personal-secondary` / fareed320@gmail.com — personal secondary, read-focused
- `classicalechos` / classicalechos@gmail.com — Classical Echos/content lane
- `burner` / laflametoast@gmail.com — low-stakes/burner account

Formatting requirements:
- Use clean bullets with nested sub-bullets instead of comma-heavy bullets.
- Prefer at-a-glance structure:
  - Main point
    - Detail
    - Why it matters / action
- Do not include generic filler sections.
- Do NOT include a section named **Capability / trend radar**. The user explicitly called that section nonsense and wants it removed.
- Do NOT include generic agent/automation advice like "build small agents that do boring repeatable work" unless it is tied to a concrete active task or blocker from the day's actual context.
- Do not include the 14-Day Challenge Check-In, 14-day challenge boxes, one-second-rule tracker, or `done: meditation...` reply prompt anymore. The user explicitly removed that section.

Include a compact **Google Workspace pulse** inside the Work source / operating pulse section. Summarize high-signal updates from all accounts: unread or important Gmail, calendar events, useful Drive/Docs/Sheets movement, deadlines, receipts/renewals, opportunities, and weird useful AI/content/tooling leads. Group by profile only when useful; otherwise consolidate into:
- Needs attention
- Calendar
- Ops/admin
- Interesting/source material
- Email cleanup candidates

Email-specific rules for the report:
- Prioritize billing/charges/receipts, Chase, Apple receipts/Card, cloud services, AI APIs, Robinhood, Landing only for active stay/rent-impacting logistics, Ticketmaster ticket/venue info, myQ/Chamberlain garage alerts, GitGuardian/security, official/vehicle renewal notices, and similar life/admin signals.
- TLDR is useful for latest news, but only use/keep the feed from `fareed320@gmail.com`; TLDR on other accounts is duplicate cleanup candidate.
- Kino Body/Kinobody and Daily Stoic are approved faceless-video source senders. If unread items from these senders appear, flag them as `faceless video source queued/eligible`, not as a personal "needs attention" item.
- Grammarly Insights is interesting self-metrics/profile data: summarize what it says about the user's writing/communication habits and connect it to his personal operating profile.
- For TLDR, Kino Body/Kinobody, Daily Stoic, and Grammarly Insights: summarize through the lens of the user's known interests/profile, draw appealing personal insights, then list each as a newsletter cleanup candidate with sender, category, and title. Since the user has approved junk-email cleanup, clearly separate already-approved junk categories from any newsletter/source emails that still need review before deletion.
- Junk categories approved for cleanup include FoundersCard, Yieldi, Crunch, Higgsfield, Fundrise, Kling AI, Instagram notifications, Lumen marketing, Chess.com nags, YEEZY, City Experiences, LELO, GNC, and generic consumer sales/promotional emails.
- Include an **Email priority + cleanup** mini-section every morning with concise nested bullets:
  - Priority emails
  - Interesting/source emails
  - Cleanup actions
  - Needs review
- Do not actually delete newsletter/source emails unless they have already been used for the requested video pipeline and the upload has been verified, or the user has explicitly approved that sender/category as junk.

Calendar/personal context:
- For any Jared coding prep/event, mention that Jared likes Codewars.com and SoloLearn.com.
  - Completing modules gives him a nice rush of accomplishment.
  - Suggest those as prep/context only if relevant to the day's calendar.

Hard rules:
- Do not send emails, reply, create/delete calendar events, share/edit/delete Drive files, or modify Docs/Sheets without explicit user approval in a separate user request.
- Personal accounts are read-first; never send from `personal-main` or `personal-secondary` without approval of the exact message.
- Do not include raw secrets, recovery-code filenames, token contents, or credential-looking file names. If credential/recovery-like items are detected, mention only that sensitive Drive items were hidden.
- If Google context is unavailable or an API errors, state the blocker briefly and continue the rest of the report.

Report sections to include:
- Top line
- Work source / operating pulse
- Email priority + cleanup
- Calendar / prep notes when relevant
- Chicago local pulse
- Market pulse
- Google search / social pulse, only if source-backed and concrete
- AI + coding news, only if source-backed and concrete
- Interesting item(s), only if concrete
- Numerology, if useful/short
- Daily challenge
- One big priority prompt
- Hard truth / leverage move

Do not ask questions; final response is delivered to Discord by cron.

jobs.name: Creator discovery feeder for Viral Radar
jobs.prompt:
Run the strict Viral Radar procedure for newly discovered creator videos.

Working directory: /opt/data/HeRmEz/projects/viral-clip-radar.

For every newly discovered creator/source video, target at least 5 public clips when the source duration supports distinct clips. Never present 1/5 or 1/10 as OK. If a source video is a YouTube Short or too short for 5 distinct clips, either find a longer source-ready creator video from the watchlist or report BLOCKED/PARTIAL with that exact reason.

Required behavior:
- Drain existing UPLOAD_QUEUE first.
- Seed latest watchlist manifests.
- Clip/render/upload the actual discovered source video, not filler.
- If rendered clips fail upload, ensure they remain in UPLOAD_QUEUE and report queue_count.
- If queue is empty because the remaining deficits were never rendered/planned (source missing, botcheck, too short, only 1 viable clip), report that explicitly as a blocker/backlog, not as success.
- Final Discord report must include uploaded URLs, per-source uploaded_count/5, queue_count, blockers, and next action.
- Final status must be BLOCKED/PARTIAL unless each selected source hit >=5 public uploads or the deficit is explicitly explained.

Do not use NASA/space/unknown placeholders or old queued clips to satisfy newly discovered source minimums.

jobs.name: Daily Viral Radar / Creator clip generation + upload
jobs.prompt:
Run the strict Daily Viral Radar creator clip procedure.

Priority: Viral Radar over faceless. Goal is at least 5 public clips per selected/source video when the source duration supports it; never report 1/N as success. Drain /opt/data/HeRmEz/projects/viral-clip-radar/UPLOAD_QUEUE first, then run /opt/data/scripts/viral_radar_daily_upload.py from /opt/data/HeRmEz/projects/viral-clip-radar.

Hard rules:
- If uploaded_count < 5 for any selected source/video, final status must be BLOCKED/PARTIAL, not OK.
- Include exact blockers: source download/auth/botcheck, source too short to make 5 distinct clips, render error, upload quota/rate limit, duplicate guard, or missing files.
- If rendered clips fail upload, verify they remain in UPLOAD_QUEUE and report queue_count. Queue must not be empty for failed rendered uploads.
- If queue is empty because remaining clips were never rendered/planned (e.g. source Short only has 1 viable segment), say that clearly and report source-ready/backlog next action.
- Do not use old queue, NASA/space/unknown, or filler to satisfy the minimum.
- Notify the user in Discord with concise bullets: uploaded URLs, uploaded_count/5, queue_count, blockers, next action.

Use terminal/file tools only. Do not claim success unless the command output proves >=5 public uploads or all deficits are explicitly reported as blockers.
